output.subject: We've received your complaint about your replacement card
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for contacting us about your replacement card. We have received your complaint, and we want to confirm that we understand the main points.

You told us that on August 20th you paid a $15 fee to have a replacement for your lost card rushed to you, with delivery expected in 2 business days. You mentioned that the card has not arrived and that the tracking shows no information. You also let us know that you fly out on 9/19 and need this resolved before you leave. You asked that either the card reach you before then or the $15 fee be returned.

We're sorry for the frustration and worry this has caused, especially with your trip coming up.

A specialist team is reviewing your complaint and will respond to you within 10 business days. If anything changes in the meantime, such as the card arriving, please reply to this email so we can add it to your complaint.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: The customer travels on 9/19. Check whether the 10-business-day response window ends after that date, and whether the customer needs to be contacted sooner.
Confirm the order date, the $15 expedite fee, and the promised 2-business-day delivery against the card order record.
Check the shipment status and why tracking shows no information. Decide whether a new card needs to be reissued or the address verified.
Decide whether to refund the $15 rush fee, which the customer requested if the card does not arrive. The draft makes no commitment either way.
Make sure the lost card has been blocked, since the customer reported it lost.
The customer included the lost card's account reference (⟦ACCOUNT_1⟧). It is deliberately left out of the reply.
